authority: Master Requirements Registry v5 SRR sheet · Ruling 5

rules.statement: External party admitted as organisation-level principal with identity, posture, terms, domain, mandate
Every request carries a party principal with its own mandate, mark state, behavioural signature
Connecting an external agent admits an autonomous non-human principal with its own stated scope
Slow-play extraction detected against cumulative history, not evaluated per request
DAP is a trust-domain boundary — no shared identifier resolution, store, or credential with the party
Browse returns aggregate composition only — never unit contents, sample, or preview
Connected workspace: party's query enters, de-identified results leave, estate data never leaves
Processed intelligence egresses derived output only; source units recorded, not reconstructable
Fine-tuning is compute-to-data only — no configuration permits the inverse
Trained weights/skill files leave as artefact egress with rights posture, hash, terms cited
Raw download is the outer-gate crossing (#25) — redaction as a gate, evidence record written
Admission of an external party is a governed act requiring the estate owner's named authority
API keys per party principal, revocable in one act, expiring, non-transferable, never logged
Controlled request routes to named approving authority before execution; does not execute pending
Approval decisions recorded with authority, decision, reason; no execution on silence
Fine-tune and skill-development always require approval; raw download always if controlled
Standing approval possible, revocable in one act, must name controlled units explicitly to cover them
Every extraction is a commissioned job with a frozen objective (#32)
Every job routes to its governing engine per §4; DAP holds no extraction logic of its own
Assistance chat may shape pre-commission; cannot approve, widen scope, or decide any gate
Every operation emits a metered event with all required fields, written before result returned
Terms resolve most-specific-first: party, then custody class, then estate default
Spend against ceiling evaluated before execution; over-ceiling routes to a person
Cumulative extraction history per party is first-class, queryable, retained for full admission
Every custody-class/operation combination defaults unavailable — availability is granted, not assumed
Owner sets terms/ceilings per custody class and party; changes never alter receipts already issued
Owner can suspend a party in one act — halts all in-flight and future operations, recorded
Every gate fails closed — no result returned when a governing check cannot complete
A metered event that cannot be written to the Ledger refuses the operation it meters
Browse degrades rather than refuses — stale data marked as stale, never presented as complete
Artefact egress distance gate — no weights/skill file leaves without passing a reproduction probe
Admission integrity for entering base models — provenance, hash, mirage behavioural probe
Every DAP operation's output passes A5.15 before return to the party (browse exempt)
Coalition membership recorded at admission; classes (a)/(b) deterministic, class (c) labelled suspicion
Estate release budget — ruled ceiling on total release across all parties/operations/time; floor violation on breach
Differentially private training (DP-SGD) by default for every fine-tune; non-DP requires approval + stricter gate

A fine-tuned artefact MAY be pruned — magnitude pruning or an equivalent structural reduction — between MOAC acceptance and DAP-31's distance gate, as a ruled optional step. Pruning is a second, empirical reduction in memorisation surface on top of DAP-36's differentially private training; it is never a substitute for it, and this document does not present it as one. A pruned artefact MUST re-pass MOAC's acceptance criteria — pruning can degrade performance below the accepted bar, and acceptance is re-evaluated, not assumed to survive the change. A pruned artefact's hash differs from its pre-pruning hash; it is a new artefact for every purpose DAP-10 and DAP-31 govern, including a fresh pass through the distance gate at the ruled threshold. Pruning ratio and method are ruled values, ratified alongside DAP-31's own probe parameters.

When a unit's rights status changes to withdrawn — consent revoked, licence expired, or an equivalent event — every artefact whose training manifest cites that unit is identified via the registry (a query, per RBM-20's design, not a search) and is either re-derived without the unit or recalled. Re-derivation trains a replacement artefact excluding the withdrawn unit, using the same run configuration recorded in the original training manifest, and passes it through DAP-31 and MOAC as a new artefact before it replaces the original in the registry. Recall withdraws the original artefact's registry entry and, where the artefact was already delivered under DAP-10, notifies the receiving party that the artefact's rights basis has changed. A unit's contribution to the estate release budget (DAP-35) is NOT refunded on unlearning — the privacy loss from the original release already occurred; unlearning restores the artefact's cleanliness going forward, not the budget already spent.
